item.title: Information-Driven Design of Imaging Systems
item.description:
BAIR researchers describe an information-theoretic approach to co-designing imaging systems, where an encoder (the optical system) maps objects to noiseless images that noise then corrupts into measurements. Their information estimator uses only the noisy measurements and a noise model to quantify how well a design captures the scene, enabling optics and reconstruction algorithms to be optimized jointly rather than separately.

item.title: RL without TD Learning: A Divide-and-Conquer Alternative
item.description:
A BAIR post introduces a reinforcement learning algorithm built on divide and conquer rather than temporal-difference learning. Unlike traditional TD methods, which bootstrap value estimates from successive states, the proposed paradigm decomposes the problem and avoids bootstrapping altogether, offering an alternative foundation for credit assignment in sequential decision making.

item.title: What Exactly Does word2vec Learn? A Theoretical Account
item.description:
BAIR researchers revisit word2vec to explain precisely what the algorithm learns and how. They frame the question as understanding representation learning in a minimal yet interesting language modeling task, using theory to characterize the embeddings that emerge from the classic method — work that connects foundational NLP results to modern questions about what language models represent internally.
